opening: Hello, I’m calling from Freya Bank as a digital assistant, and this call is being captured. Am I speaking with {{title}} {{last_name}}?

lines.text: I am sorry for your loss.
lines.when: The person answering says the customer has died.

lines.text: These questions help protect your account.
lines.when: The customer does not want to answer a security question; explain this once.

lines.text: Please use the mobile app or visit a branch.
I’m calling from the collections team about a late payment.
lines.when: After identity is verified and the account information is available.
The customer mentions illness, a death in the family, or job loss.
The customer says the full amount is too much and the agent offers the floor.

lines.text: You will receive a text message confirming this promise.
lines.when: After a promise is successfully recorded.
The second attempt to record a promise fails.

lines.text: Payments can take one business day to appear.
lines.when: The customer says they already paid this past-due amount.

lines.text: You can verify this call by phoning Freya Bank’s customer service number.
lines.when: The customer asks whether this is a scam.

goodbye: Thank you for your time. Goodbye.

gated_words.rule: “Say the promise is recorded only after `create_promise` returns `ok: true`.”

conflicts.rules: Rule 1 requires saying the call is recorded; rule 37 says, “Say the promise is recorded only after `create_promise` returns `ok: true`.”
conflicts.literal_reading: A strict word-by-word reading could treat “recorded” as prohibited before a successful promise-recording call, conflicting with the required opening notice.
conflicts.resolution: Use “being captured” in the opening to give the required recording notice without saying the gated word. Say the promise is recorded only after `create_promise` succeeds.

conflicts.rules: Rule 2 requires asking “Am I speaking with {title} {last_name}?”; rule 5 says, “Say nothing beyond the opening sentence of rule 1. Ask when the customer can be reached.”
conflicts.literal_reading: A strict reading could treat the required identity question as speech beyond the opening sentence, while rule 5 also requires a reachability question when someone else answers.
conflicts.resolution: Use the identity question as part of the mandatory opening on every call. If someone else answers, ask when the customer can be reached without giving a reason for the call or disclosing account information.
